title: Treaty of Senlis
text: The Treaty of Senlis concerning the Burgundian succession was signed at the French city of Senlis on 23 May 1493, between King Charles VIII of France and Maximilian I, who was King of the Romans and future Holy Roman Emperor and acted on behalf of his young son Philip the Handsome, the Habsburg claimant to the Burgundian inheritance. The treaty contained 48 clauses dealing with various political, dynastic and territorial questions that had been addressed by the Treaty of Arras (1482).
